verdicts.evidence: Independently re-ran `grep -rniE "mmd|\.svg|\.png|excalidraw|diagram skill|render|editable|source file|drift|stale|commit"` across SKILL.md and all five references/*.md — zero matches, confirming the original search. SKILL.md:73 and :84-92 show the skill's diagram output is only ever an inline fenced Mermaid block.
verdicts.reasoning: The absence-search is accurate: architecture-designer never mentions a .mmd/.svg pair, excalidraw, or a 'diagram skill'. However, I reclassify from unenforced-gap to load-bearing-parameter: this is not a gap in architecture-designer's own behavior, because that behavior was never architecture-designer's to own. A dedicated skill exists at plugins/dev-kit-core/skills/diagram/SKILL.md whose description is exactly this contract ('Authors mermaid from a plain-English request, renders it to SVG/PNG, and keeps the .mmd source as the editable single source of truth (plus an optional .excalidraw scene)') and whose body fully specifies the committed source+render artifact pair, the render fallback chain, and the 'never edit the SVG/PNG directly' rule. KICKOFF's instruction to 'use the diagram skill for the architecture diagrams' is a cross-skill routing decision (which of two available skills produces this artifact) plus a cross-artifact sync reminder — squarely the rubric's 'which other artifact to feed in as context' / 'ordering across skills' non-duplication bullets, not evidence that architecture-designer fails to enforce its own contract. It is still load-bearing text that must be kept (no single skill could know to route diagram production elsewhere and keep the two outputs in sync), so the underlying finding survives, but 'unenforced-gap' mischaracterizes it as a defect in architecture-designer when it is normal, correct division of labor between two named skills. Severity kept at medium given the real operational risk described (nothing downstream catches a stale .mmd/.svg pair).
